notes: {"answer":"Call 911 now. Swelling of the lips and face, hives and a hoarse voice after peanuts are an emergency. If your child has an epinephrine auto-injector, use it right away. Don't wait to see if it passes. Keep them lying down and stay with them.","triage":"Call 911 now, not 811. Antihistamines are not a substitute for epinephrine. If symptoms don't improve in about 5 minutes and you have a second auto-injector, 911 can advise on using it. Even if your child looks better, they still need the ER, because symptoms can come back.","sources":["Food Allergy Canada","KidsHealth","Cleveland Clinic","American Academy of Pediatrics"]}
